summary: Order quote timeouts are caused by the pricing-engine feature-flag ramp cfg-3120 (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5→100 at 12:04:00Z). Enabling GreeksV2 for all traffic made every quote run the expensive GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo path (20000 paths, 3–9s per call), blowing the 2000ms quote budget. pricing-engine p99 jumped from ~60ms to ~2.6s in the 12:05 bucket and order-service quote timeouts + 8% error rate began at 12:06. The reported market-data-service protobuf deploy (dep-6111 at 11:56) is NOT the cause: market-data-service p99 stayed flat at ~40ms across the entire window. Root cause is a config/feature-flag change (config_change) in pricing-engine.

ranked_hypotheses.title: GreeksV2 feature-flag ramp to 100% overloads pricing-engine quote computation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 (greeks_v2 rollout_pct 5→100 at 12:04) forced all quote requests onto the expensive GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo path (20000 paths, 3–9s each), exceeding the 2000ms budget. pricing-engine quote latency rose to ~2.6s p99, causing downstream order-service quote calls to time out at 2500ms.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3120 ramps greeks_v2 from 5% to 100% at 12:04:00Z
All quotes now run GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo (20000 paths, multi-second) from 12:05:21Z
Quote requests exceed the 2000ms budget -> pricing-engine deadline-exceeded errors
pricing-engine p99 latency jumps 60ms -> 2.6s in the 12:05 bucket
order-service quote calls exceed their 2500ms client timeout, error rate rises to ~8%

assumptions: cfg-3120 greeks_v2 metric actually routes traffic to GreeksV2Calculator (naming correlation only)
No pricing-engine code deploy occurred (confirmed: 0 deployments)

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy slows quotes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-6111 switched market-data-service quote serialization to protobuf at 11:56, which the incident report suspected caused quote timeouts.
assumptions: protobuf change could affect downstream quote latency
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service p99 stayed flat at ~40ms across the entire window (F6); the deploy at 11:56 was 9 minutes before onset, whereas the symptom onset (12:05-12:06) aligns exactly with cfg-3120 at 12:04. No market-data-service degradation observed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load/CPU saturation of pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A surge in quote request volume saturated pricing-engine CPU, inflating latency.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate was flat (~640 req/s) at onset (F9) and memory_pct was stable (F10); latency rose ~40x in one bucket without any traffic increase — a per-request cost change, not load.

facts.statement: order-service reported 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' errors beginning 2026-05-20T12:06:10Z.
A pricing-engine feature-flag change cfg-3120 (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5→100) took effect at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z.
pricing-engine GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo warnings (20000 paths, 3–9s) began 12:05:21Z, one minute after cfg-3120.
pricing-engine p99 latency jumped from ~59ms to ~2609ms in the 12:05 bucket and stayed elevated.
order-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6.93% in the 12:05 bucket.
market-data-service p99 latency remained flat (~40ms) throughout, ruling out its protobuf deploy as the cause.
pricing-engine request_rate was flat and memory_pct stable at onset, excluding load/memory saturation.

assumptions: The greeks_v2 rollout flag controls whether quotes use GreeksV2Calculator (inferred from naming and a 1-minute timing alignment).
No pricing-engine code deployment occurred (confirmed: 0 deployments in window), so latency increase is due to the flag change, not new code.
No other simultaneous change on unresponsive config-audit shard 2/3 occurred.

timeline.event: market-data-service emits a deprecated TLS cipher WARN (benign noise).
dep-6111: market-data-service v5.2.0 protobuf serialization deployed (suspected by report, later ruled out).
pricing-engine GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo warnings begin (3–9s per call).
pricing-engine p99 jumps to 2609.71ms; order-service error_rate jumps to 6.93%.
First order-service 'quote call timed out after 2500ms' error.
First pricing-engine 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2'.
pricing-engine p99 still ~2.6s; incident unresolved as of latest data.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately revert cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0).
recommended_actions.rationale: The flag ramp is the trigger; rollback should restore pricing-engine p99 to ~60ms and clear order-service timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery by watching pricing-engine latency_p99_ms and order-service quote-timeout log volume for 10 minutes after the flag revert.
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms the causal chain and that no second factor (e.g. a memory backlog) persists.

recommended_actions.action: Before re-enabling, benchmark GreeksV2Calculator and reduce Monte-Carlo paths or move it off the synchronous quote path (cache/async).
recommended_actions.rationale: 20000-path Monte-Carlo at 3–9s cannot meet the 2000ms synchronous budget; the feature is inherently too costly inline.

recommended_actions.action: Add a rollout guardrail: auto-halt a feature-flag ramp if pricing-engine p99 or deadline-exceeded rate crosses a threshold.
recommended_actions.rationale: A 5%→100% jump in one step caused a 40x latency regression; staged ramps with automated abort would have caught it.

recommended_actions.action: Add a per-request latency budget check before routing to console the Greeks calculator so slow paths degrade gracefully instead of timing out downstream callers.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents an expensive optional computation from breaking the quote SLA for all callers.

data_gaps: pricing-engine cpu_pct metric could not be retrieved (upstream timeout, 3 attempts) — CPU saturation as a contributory factor is unverified, though request_rate and memory were flat.
pricing-engine error_rate metric could not be retrieved (upstream timeout) — deadline-exceeded rate confirmed only via logs, not metrics.
First config-change query returned partial:true (config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond); a retry returned only cfg-3120, so a concurrent change on a third of shards cannot be fully excluded.
market-data-service config-change query timed out (3 attempts) — no market-data-service config changes were confirmed, only inferred from the absence of correlated latency.
No direct metric linking greeks_v2 flag value to GreeksV2Calculator invocation exists; the link is name-based correlation plus exact timing alignment.
